title: Genome-wide association meta-analysis of eating behavior traits revealed one susceptibility locus for emotional eating
title_zh: 全基因组关联meta分析揭示情绪进食一个易感位点
abstract: In order to identify new and genome-wide significant loci for eating behavior traits (cognitive restraint, uncontrolled eating and emotional eating), we conducted a meta-GWAS with seven studies of European ancestry (n = 11,250). Eating behavior was assessed using the Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire. Genotype effects of single studies were estimated using additive models adjusting for age, sex, BMI, and principal components and single study results were combined by fixed-effect meta-analysis. For cognitive restraint and uncontrolled eating, no genome-wide significant association could be detected. For emotional eating, one genomic region on chromosome 5 comprising two polymorphisms attained genome-wide significance (P = 4.0×10-8 for rs6877636 and P = 3.2×10−8 for rs6897090). The minor alleles were associated with higher emotional eating scores (β=0.093 ± 0.017), with a similar direction of effect in each study. Both SNPs, in near perfect linkage disequilibrium, mapped to RP11-24P24.1, a processed pseudogene of ornithine decarboxylase 1 (ODC1). Enrichment analysis revealed a significant overlap between genome-wide BMI-associated variants and nominal emotional eating variants, supporting the hypothesis that shared genetic factors may influence both eating behavior traits and obesity risk. Finally, we observed a number of interesting associations reaching suggestive significance (P < 10−6) involving BMI candidate genes, including a suggestive association between FTO variants and cognitive restraint (rs9922708, β = 0.069, P = 5.9×10−7). In conclusion, our meta-GWAS identified for the first time a robust chromosomal region associated with emotional eating in seven studies. Given that emotional eating strongly influences body weight but is often stigmatized, recognizing genetic susceptibility to certain eating behaviors may help reduce stigma and alleviate guilt.
abstract_zh: 为了识别认知抑制、失控进食和情绪进食等饮食行为特征的新基因组显著位点，我们进行了一项包含七项欧洲血统研究的meta-GWAS（n = 11,250）。使用三因素饮食问卷评估饮食行为。单项研究的基因型效应使用调整年龄、性别、BMI和主成分的加性模型估计，并通过固定效应meta分析合并单项研究结果。对于认知抑制和失控进食，未检测到基因组显著关联。对于情绪进食，染色体5上一个包含两个多态性的基因组区域达到了基因组显著性（rs6877636 P = 4.0×10-8 和 rs6897090 P = 3.2×10−8）。 minor 等位基因与较高的情绪进食评分相关联（β=0.093 ± 0.017），每项研究的效应方向相似。这两个SNP在近乎完美的连锁不平衡中，映射到RP11-24P24.1，这是鸟氨酸羧化酶1（ODC1）的加工伪基因。富集分析揭示了基因组BMI相关变异与情绪进食的基因组显著变异之间的显著重叠，支持共同的遗传因子可能同时影响饮食行为特征和肥胖风险的假设。最后，我们观察到了许多达到建议显著性水平（P < 10−6）的有趣关联，涉及BMI候选基因，包括FTO变异与认知抑制之间的建议关联（rs9922708, β = 0.069, P = 5.9×10−7）。总之，我们的meta-GWAS首次在七项研究中确定了与情绪进食相关的稳健染色体区域。鉴于情绪进食显著影响体体重但常被污名化，识别某些饮食行为的遗传易感性可能有助于减少污名化并缓解内疚感。
